title: Philippine National Bank v. Court of Appeals
summary: The Supreme Court reaffirmed that the relationship between a bank and its depositor is one of creditor-debtor. Banks are required to exercise the highest degree of diligence in handling deposits and are liable for damages when they fail to return deposits on demand.
doctrine: The bank-depositor relationship is that of creditor and debtor. The bank has the obligation to return the deposit upon demand. Banks must exercise extraordinary diligence because of the fiduciary nature of banking. The degree of diligence required is more than that of a good father of a family.
fullText:
MELO, J.:

This case involves a claim by a depositor against the bank for the unauthorized withdrawal from the depositor's savings account.

The relationship between a bank and its depositors is that of creditor-debtor. The deposit under the account of the depositor creates a contractual obligation on the part of the bank to pay the depositor upon demand. The bank's failure to return the deposit upon demand constitutes a breach of this obligation.

The business of banking is imbued with public interest. The stability of banks depends on the confidence of the people in the honesty and efficiency of banks. Banks are required to exercise the highest degree of diligence in the selection and supervision of their employees and in the handling of their clients' accounts.
